findings.title: [P1] Restrict redirects to approved same-origin destinations
findings.body: When `returnUrl` originates from a query parameter or other untrusted input, passing it directly to `location.assign` permits redirects to attacker-controlled sites and potentially `javascript:` navigation. Parse and restrict it to approved same-origin HTTP(S) destinations before navigating.

findings.title: [P1] Stop recording issued tokens in logs
findings.body: Every token passed to `recordIssuedToken` is written verbatim through `console.log`. In environments that retain or aggregate console output, anyone with log access can recover and replay a still-valid credential. Audit only non-sensitive metadata or a safely redacted identifier.

findings.title: [P1] Restrict `returnUrl` to validated same-origin destinations
findings.body:
Passing an attacker-controlled `returnUrl` such as `https://attacker.example` creates an open redirect; a `javascript:` URL can execute script in the page context where CSP permits it. This bites when the login callback obtains the return URL from a query parameter or other untrusted input.

_Recommend validating this comment independently._

findings.title: [P2] Redact issued tokens before auditing
findings.body:
Every live token passed to `recordIssuedToken` is forwarded to `audit`, which writes it verbatim to the console. In deployments that persist or aggregate console output, anyone with log access can recover active credentials and impersonate users.

_Recommend validating this comment independently._

findings.title: [P1] Validate `returnUrl` before assigning it to `location`
findings.body:
If the post-login return URL is attacker-controlled, values such as `javascript:...` can execute script in the application origin, while `https://attacker.example` creates an open redirect. Restrict redirects to approved same-origin HTTP(S) paths.

_Recommend validating this comment independently._

findings.title: [P1] Stop writing issued tokens to console logs
findings.body:
Every issued token is passed directly to `console.log`. In environments where stdout/browser logs are retained or accessible to support staff, log processors, or other users, a still-valid bearer token can be recovered and replayed.

_Recommend validating this comment independently._
